Decay chain of a body

Source: R/tph.R
tpdmc.Rd

A discrete-time Markov chain of decomposition: from each transient stage (fresh, bloat, active and advanced decay, or the user's own stages) a body advances to the next stage with probability decay * (1 - pres) (after the last, to skeletal), mummifies with probability mum * pres, and otherwise stays. pres is the strength of what preserves the body (aridity, quicklime, a sealed casket), 0 for none. From the fundamental matrix come the probability of ending skeletal or mummified from each stage and the expected steps to get there. With no preservation nothing mummifies, so the column mummified of absorb is also the change in the chance of mummifying that the preservation makes. With steps above 0 one path is drawn from start.

Usage

tpdmc(
  pres = 0,
  decay = 0.5,
  mum = 0.5,
  states = c("fresh", "bloat", "active", "advanced"),
  start = 1,
  steps = 0,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

pres

The preservation: one number from 0 to 1.

decay

The chance to advance a stage without preservation: one number above 0, at most 1.

mum

The chance to mummify at full preservation: one number from 0 to 1.

states

The names of the transient stages, in order.

start

The stage a drawn path starts from: a name of states or its number.

steps

The longest path drawn (it stops when absorbed): one whole number from 0, 0 for none.

seed

NULL (the draws follow set.seed()) or a whole number from 0.

Value

A list: P, the transition matrix (stages, then skeletal and mummified); N, the fundamental matrix of the transient stages; absorb, the probability of ending skeletal or mummified from each stage; time, the expected steps to absorption from each stage; start; path, NULL or the states of the drawn path.

References

Kemeny, J. G. and Snell, J. L. (1960). Finite Markov Chains. Van Nostrand.

Examples

tpdmc(pres = 0.4)$absorb
#>          skeletal mummified
#> fresh      0.1296    0.8704
#> bloat      0.2160    0.7840
#> active     0.3600    0.6400
#> advanced   0.6000    0.4000
tpdmc(pres = 0.4, steps = 50, seed = 1)$path
#> [1] "fresh"     "fresh"     "mummified"
